Subject: Amortization split question for on‑prem pilot

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're pushing this through procurement and legal and have one commercial question we need clarified before we can raise a PO: how is Redwood splitting the commercial construct between the platform fee (amortized) and the operator/site licenses? Specifically:

- We need a 36‑month amortization profile for the platform fee to show in our CAPEX request.
- For operator licenses: can we get an option to move 40% of operator license cost into a short pilot discount, rather than upfront?

Can you send a clean SOW showing both line items separated, plus the version with the pilot discount carved out? Legal also asked for a sample redline of the license section they can review.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we have a finance window next week.

Thanks,
Sarah Lin
Procurement Manager
Acme Health

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Quick read below and attaching a first pass SOW that separates the platform amortization line and the operator license SKU table (Acme_SOW_v1.2.pdf).

Summary of options in the SOW:
- Platform fee: one line, list price and suggested 36‑month amortization schedule in appendix A.
- Operator licenses: per‑site operator SKU + optional pilot credit line.
- Pilot option (recommended): 10% off operator license rate for the first 3 months + ability to convert credits into node discounts on conversion.

Two asks from our side before I lock numbers:
1) Kimberly: please confirm whether we can carve a 40% deferral into a short trial credit (convertible on signature) or whether we should present it as an upfront discount.
2) David: confirm SRE support bandings and the cost delta for 24x7 vs business hours (we quoted BH in the doc).

If we agree internally today I can send a revised offer to you with the DocuSign link.

Best,

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Amortization split question for on‑prem pilot (internal)

Lukas — internal notes below. Keeping it short so you have something to send to Acme.

- Pilot credit vs deferral: Legal likes a credit instrument (discount applied to pilot invoices, convertible to license credit on conversion). That avoids CAPEX/expense ambiguity. We can support up to 40% conversion credits, but not as a deferral on the platform fee — platform fee needs to be treated as a separate subscription amortized over the term.

- Discount sizing: For a clean procurement path propose
  * Pilot operator discount: 30% on operator SKU for months 1–3 (instead of 40% ask). 30% is defensible and keeps ARR sensible on conversion.
  * Platform fee amortization: provide the 36‑month schedule (line in SOW) with an optional upfront discount of 5% if they commit to a 36‑month purchase order.

- Support tiers: Acme asked about 24x7. We should price 24x7 as an add‑on. If they pick 24x7 for pilot sites we can offer a one‑time implementation credit to offset ramp issues (up to $12k).

David — I flagged the SRE cost delta in comments of the SOW (redline). Can you confirm numbers by EOD?

Kimberly
Head of Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference

Subject: Offer update: pilot credit + amortization schedule (SOW attached)

Hi Sarah & Carlos — following up with the updated commercial construct based on our internal review. Key points (high level):

- Pilot credit: 30% operator discount applied to months 1–3 for up to 4 pilot sites. Credit is applied to Redwood invoices during pilot and is convertible to operator license credit on contract conversion (up to 40% max conversion cap).
- Platform fee: shown as a separate line in the SOW with a 36‑month amortization schedule in Appendix A. We included a 5% prepay discount if Acme signs a 36‑month PO at execution.
- Support: BH (business hours) included. 24x7 offered as an add‑on; pricing in SOW. Implementation credit: one‑time $12,000 credit if they opt for 24x7 on pilot scope.

Attached: Acme_SOW_v1.2.pdf (commercial table + appendix), and a ready DocuSign offer PDF linked below for convenience.

Quote valid for 14 days. Happy to hop on a short call today if you want to run the finance team through the amortization table.
